title: Minimax Estimation of Generalized-Wald Impulse Responses for Point Processes with Weak Instruments
banked_reason: The mean-shift assumption holds almost surely for each fixed pair of treatment times, but the identification proof substitutes the random pair (T1,T0); that substitution does not follow.

proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a same-subject spectral covariance calculation, explicit causal lower experiments, and claimed matching weak-IV minimax and honest-diameter frontiers for bounded-path and BV/counting outcomes. D0.5 found an atomless null-graph counterexample: fixed-pair almost-sure mean-shift statements do not support substitution of the random treatment-time pair, so the identification bridge and all decaying upper-frontier headlines are false under the stated class. The sound same-assumption residue is only incremental positive-strength nonidentification/constant risk; restoring the intended frontier requires a transparently stronger realized-pair or joint-version assumption, and the fractional Sobolev reconstruction proof also remains incomplete.
tldr: With complete paired treatment and outcome trajectories, the squared-\(L^2\) minimax and fixed-smoothness honest-diameter orders for the causal generalized-Wald impulse are \(1\wedge(n\kappa^2)^{-s/(s+1)}\) for bounded càdlàg paths and \(1\wedge(n\kappa^2)^{-2s/(2s+1)}\) for bounded-variation paths. Both classes are uniformly learnable exactly when \(n\kappa_n^2\to\infty\). The matched lower laws are causal full-data experiments in a sufficient explicitly proved scaled truncated-exponential richness regime: some fixed \(d,\lambda>0\) satisfy \(d\kappa_0<1\), \(c\le d(1-e^{-\lambda A})/\max(1,\lambda)\), and \(C\ge d(1+e^{-\lambda A})/\min(1,\lambda)\). This ratio restriction is sufficient for the present witness, not claimed necessary.
gap: Generalized-Wald identification and a penalized estimator exist, but their weak-first-stage full-path risk and honest-inference frontiers have not been established in the inspected source. Generic inverse-problem rates do not account for the paired transform covariance or the information in complete counting paths.
fill: Establish matching class-specific minimax and honest-diameter rates by paired residual-spectrum upper bounds and full-observation causal lower experiments, including an exact nonlearning threshold.
